name: Production Incident Response
description: Restore service first without destroying the evidence needed to understand why it failed.

tasks.name: Declare and bound incident
tasks.objective: Confirm impact, affected users/services/regions, severity, start time, current symptoms, data/security implications, incident channel, commander, and evidence-preservation needs.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Scope and severity are stated as current evidence, not guesswork.

tasks.name: Stabilize service
tasks.objective: Choose the lowest-risk reversible containment or rollback that reduces user harm. Freeze risky concurrent changes and record every intervention with timestamp and observed effect.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Mitigations are reversible where practical and their effects are measured.

tasks.name: Build evidence timeline and diagnose
tasks.objective: Correlate deploys, configuration, feature flags, dependencies, metrics, traces, logs, queues, resource pressure, security events, and operator actions. Maintain competing hypotheses and avoid changing evidence solely to make graphs look normal.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Timeline separates facts, hypotheses, and interventions.

tasks.name: Restore and verify
tasks.objective: Apply the smallest durable correction needed for service restoration, verify user-visible recovery and backlog/data integrity, then cautiously remove temporary mitigations.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Recovery is verified from user/service outcomes, not only one dashboard.

tasks.name: Reconcile communications
tasks.objective: Produce concise internal/external updates that distinguish known impact, mitigations, recovery state, and unknowns. Correct earlier assumptions when evidence changes.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Status language does not claim root cause before root cause is established.

tasks.name: Postmortem and corrective actions
tasks.objective: Explain trigger, contributing conditions, detection gaps, decision points, blast radius, why defenses failed, what reduced harm, and corrective actions with owners/evidence. Avoid monocausal blame and action-item confetti.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Corrective actions map to demonstrated failure mechanisms or detection gaps.
The postmortem preserves uncertainty where causality remains unproven.
